BRA.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~169 Mt (record), domestic use ~58.5 Mt (crush ~55-57 Mt + seed/feed), exports ~110.5 Mt, small imports ~0.5 Mt. ABIOVE puts the crop near 169 Mt and exports ~106-112 Mt.

USA.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~118.8 Mt (4.37 bn bu), crush ~67 Mt (record), whole-bean exports ~50.8 Mt (USSEC: 51.2 Mt), imports ~0.4 Mt. China was ~27 Mt of US exports in CY2024.

ARG.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~49-50 Mt, crush ~40-42 Mt (world's largest), whole-bean exports only ~5 Mt because beans are crushed into meal/oil; imports ~6 Mt of beans (mostly Paraguay) feed the crush. Argentina is the top soymeal & soyoil exporter (~30-40% of world meal trade).

CHN.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: domestic prod ~20.7 Mt, total use ~125-128 Mt, crush ~100 Mt; imports ~109-112 Mt (USDA). China General Administration of Customs reported ~105 Mt for CY2024. China is ~60% of world soybean imports.

PRY.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~10.7 Mt, crush ~4 Mt, whole-bean exports ~6.3 Mt. Roughly 80% of bean exports go overland to Argentina's crush; remainder to EU, Brazil, Russia.

CAN.note: Soy Canada / USDA MY2024/25: prod ~7 Mt, crush ~2.5 Mt, exports ~4.3 Mt (identity-preserved food beans + commodity). Key markets: China, US, EU, Japan, Iran.

IND.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~12.5 Mt, crush ~11-12 Mt for domestic meal/oil; India is essentially self-contained in beans (imports restricted on GM grounds), a small net importer of edible oils not beans.

URY.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~3.3 Mt, almost entirely exported (~2.9 Mt); China and Argentina (for crush) are the main destinations. Uruguay barely crushes domestically.

RUS.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: Far East prod ~7 Mt exported to China; European Russia imports ~2.4 Mt (Brazil/Paraguay) for crush. Net importer of beans overall.

EU.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: EU-27 crushes ~15-16 Mt; domestic prod ~2.9 Mt; imports ~13-14 Mt of beans (Brazil ~39%, US, Ukraine, Canada). The EU also imports ~18 Mt of soymeal separately.

MEX.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: minimal domestic prod, imports ~6.5-6.9 Mt for crush/feed; the US supplies the overwhelming majority (~5.2 Mt to Mexico in MY24/25 per USSEC). Brazil supplies the balance.

EGY.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: imports ~3.5-4 Mt for a growing domestic crush; US (~3.3 Mt in MY24/25, USSEC) and Brazil/Argentina compete for the market.

THA.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: imports ~4-4.5 Mt for crush/feed; Brazil supplies ~78% of Thailand's bean imports (Iowa FB/Comtrade), the US most of the rest.

JPN.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: imports ~3.2-3.4 Mt for food (tofu, miso, natto) and crush; the US is the dominant supplier (~2.2 Mt in MY24/25, USSEC), Brazil and Canada the rest.

IDN.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: imports ~2.5-2.7 Mt mostly for tempeh/tofu food use; the US is the leading supplier (~2.16 Mt in MY24/25, USSEC), with Brazil/Argentina supplementing.

TUR.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: imports ~3-3.4 Mt for crush/feed; Brazil is the main supplier, with US volumes up sharply in MY24/25 (USSEC: US to Turkey +331% to ~0.83 Mt).

TWN.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: imports ~2.5-2.7 Mt for crush and food; the US and Brazil are the two main suppliers, with Taiwan a long-standing US food-grade soybean buyer.

VNM.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: imports ~1.8-2.1 Mt for feed crush; Brazil and the US are the principal suppliers.

PAK.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: imports ~1.5-2 Mt for poultry-feed crush (volume volatile on GMO-import policy); the US and Brazil are the main suppliers.

BGD.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: imports ~1.5-1.7 Mt for poultry feed; the US and South America supply the crush.

IRN.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: imports ~1.5 Mt (sanctions/finance make volumes lumpy); Brazil is the dominant supplier of beans to Iran, with Canada and Russia also shipping.

KOR.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: imports ~1.3-1.4 Mt for food and crush; the US, Brazil and at times China supply the market.

UKR.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~6.5 Mt, exports ~3-3.5 Mt mostly to the EU and Turkey; a growing European-supply alternative to the Americas.

DZA.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: imports ~1 Mt for a new domestic crush; Brazil and Canada are key suppliers to Algeria.

COL.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: imports ~1 Mt for feed/crush; the US and Brazil are the main suppliers to Colombia.

BOL.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: prod ~3 Mt, mostly crushed domestically into meal/oil for export; modest whole-bean exports to neighbours and Argentina's crush.

flows.note: China imported ~74.6 Mt of Brazilian soybeans in CY2024 (~71% of China's ~105 Mt total), per China Customs / SCMP; corroborated by ABIOVE/Brazil customs at ~73-75 Mt (~71-76% of Brazil's exports). This is the single largest bilateral flow in global agriculture. ~US$33-35bn.
China imported ~22 Mt of US soybeans in CY2024 (~21% of China's total); US data put MY2023/24 shipments to China near 27 Mt. The flow collapsed late-2025 amid tariffs but CY2024 was still large.
Brazil supplies ~39% of the EU's ~13.5 Mt of bean imports (Iowa FB/Comtrade); ~5-5.5 Mt for EU crush, the EU's single largest bean supplier.
The EU imported ~6 Mt of US soybeans in MY2024/25, up ~23% y/y (USSEC); the US is the EU's second-largest supplier after Brazil.
Mexico bought ~5.21 Mt of US soybeans in MY2024/25 (USSEC) — Mexico is the #2 destination for US soy after China, supplied almost entirely by the US.
Egypt imported ~3.34 Mt of US soybeans in MY2024/25, up ~23% y/y (USSEC); the US is Egypt's leading bean supplier.
Japan imported ~2.17 Mt of US soybeans in MY2024/25 (USSEC); the US dominates Japan's food-grade and crush bean supply.
Indonesia imported ~2.16 Mt of US soybeans in MY2024/25 (USSEC); the US is the leading supplier for Indonesia's tempeh/tofu food market.
Paraguay sends ~80% of its bean exports overland to Argentina's crush; Argentina imported ~3.3 Mt from Paraguay in the first 9 months of 2025 alone (Iowa FB/Comtrade), full-year ~4-5 Mt.
~80% of Argentina's whole-bean exports go to China (Iowa FB/Comtrade); volume modest (~3 Mt) because most of Argentina's crop is crushed domestically into meal/oil for export.
Spain is the largest single EU-member bean importer and Brazil's top EU destination after the bloc total; ~3-4 Mt for Iberian crush (USDA/Comtrade basis).
Brazil supplies ~78% of Thailand's ~4.3 Mt of bean imports (Iowa FB/Comtrade 5-yr partner share) = ~3.35 Mt; Thailand is one of Brazil's larger non-China markets.
Brazil is Turkey's main bean supplier (~2.5 Mt of Turkey's ~3.3 Mt imports); curated from USDA PSD and Comtrade partner shares.
Brazil is Iran's dominant bean supplier (~1.4 Mt); Comtrade flows are lumpy due to sanctions/finance but Brazil consistently leads (USDA PSD basis).
Russian Far East beans (~1-1.3 Mt) ship to northern China; a small but growing non-Americas supply line for China (USDA PSD basis).
China is historically Canada's top bean destination (~1.3 Mt); identity-preserved and commodity beans (Soy Canada / Comtrade basis).
In 2025 the US became Canada's top bean destination (Iowa FB/Comtrade); integrated North American oilseed market, ~0.8 Mt.
Japan is a steady buyer of Canadian food-grade (non-GM) soybeans (~0.5 Mt); Soy Canada / Comtrade basis.
The EU buys Canadian (often non-GM / sustainability-certified) beans for crush, ~0.7 Mt (Soy Canada / Comtrade basis).
Ukraine ships the bulk of its ~3.3 Mt exports to the EU and Turkey; ~1.8 Mt to EU crushers, a growing nearby alternative to the Americas (USDA PSD basis).
Turkey is a major buyer of Ukrainian beans (~0.8 Mt) via the Black Sea (USDA PSD / Comtrade basis).
Taiwan is a long-standing US food-grade bean buyer; ~1.5 Mt of Taiwan's ~2.6 Mt imports from the US (USDA/Comtrade basis).
Brazil supplies the balance of Taiwan's crush beans (~1 Mt) alongside the US (USDA/Comtrade basis).
US soybean shipments to Turkey jumped ~331% to ~0.83 Mt in MY2024/25 (USSEC), as Turkey diversified suppliers.
Brazil and the US split Vietnam's ~2 Mt of feed-crush bean imports; ~1.1 Mt from Brazil (USDA/Comtrade basis).
The US supplies the balance of Vietnam's bean imports (~0.7 Mt) alongside Brazil (USDA/Comtrade basis).
Brazil and the US supply Pakistan's ~1.9 Mt poultry-feed crush; ~1 Mt from Brazil (USDA/Comtrade basis; volumes swing on GMO-import policy).
The US supplies a large share of Pakistan's crush beans (~0.7 Mt) when import policy permits (USDA/Comtrade basis).
Brazil and the US supply Bangladesh's ~1.6 Mt feed crush; ~0.8 Mt from Brazil (USDA/Comtrade basis).
Brazil supplies part of Egypt's ~4 Mt crush alongside the US-led volume (USDA/Comtrade basis).
Brazil and Canada supply Algeria's new ~1 Mt domestic crush; ~0.6 Mt from Brazil (USDA/Comtrade basis).
European Russia imports ~2.4 Mt of beans for crush; Brazil and Paraguay are the main suppliers, ~1.2 Mt from Brazil (USDA/Comtrade basis).
Paraguay supplies part of Russia's crush imports (~0.7 Mt) alongside Brazil (USDA/Comtrade basis).
Beyond Argentina, Paraguay ships beans to EU crushers (~0.7 Mt) and Brazil (USDA/Comtrade basis).
China is Uruguay's main bean destination (~1.7 Mt of ~2.9 Mt exports); the rest goes to Argentina's crush and the EU (USDA/Comtrade basis).
Uruguay ships beans across the river to Argentina's crush (~0.7 Mt) (USDA/Comtrade basis).
Bolivia's modest whole-bean exports feed Argentina's crush and neighbouring markets (~0.2 Mt) (USDA/Comtrade basis).
The US is South Korea's leading bean supplier (~0.8 Mt of ~1.35 Mt) for food and crush (USDA/Comtrade basis).
The US supplies the non-Brazil share of Thailand's crush (~0.9 Mt) (USDA/Comtrade basis).
The US supplies part of Bangladesh's feed crush (~0.7 Mt) alongside Brazil (USDA/Comtrade basis).
The US is a leading supplier to Colombia's ~1 Mt feed/crush market (USDA/Comtrade basis).

rankings.note: Whole-soybean (HS 1201) export/import volumes in kt, USDA FAS PSD Oilseeds MY2024/25. Note Argentina ranks low on BEAN exports despite a giant crop because it crushes domestically and leads the world in soymeal/soyoil exports (not counted here). China alone is ~60% of world bean imports.

companies.name: Cargill
companies.metric: Group revenue ~US$160bn (FY2024); the world's largest private agricultural trader; soy origination/crush a core segment.
companies.note: One of the 'ABCD' traders. Major soybean origination and crushing in the US, Brazil and Argentina; large Brazil export-terminal footprint. Private, so per-commodity disclosure is limited.
companies.improve: As a private company, Cargill's soy-specific volumes and deforestation exposure are opaque. It should publish bean-origination geography (Cerrado/Amazon vs. consolidated US), EUDR-traceability coverage, and crush-margin segment data so the market can size its exposure to the Brazil-China axis.

companies.name: Archer-Daniels-Midland (ADM)
companies.metric: Revenue ~US$85.5bn (FY2024, down ~10% y/y); Ag Services & Oilseeds is the largest segment; global soy crush leader.
companies.note: One of the 'ABCD'. Soybean crushing across the US, South America and the EU; oilseed margins compressed in 2024 on abundant supply (ADM 10-K).
companies.improve: ADM should break out soy-origination by biome and report EUDR-readiness for its South American supply, plus per-region crush-margin sensitivity, so investors can separate its US-feedstock business from its Brazil/Argentina deforestation-linked exposure.

companies.name: Bunge Global (Bunge-Viterra)
companies.metric: World's largest oilseed processor; Bunge-Viterra merger completed Jul 2025, creating a ~US$50-60bn-revenue agribusiness with leading global soy crush capacity.
companies.note: One of the 'ABCD'. The merger with Viterra makes Bunge the largest global oilseed crusher; very large Brazil and Argentina soy footprint (Bunge 10-K / merger filings).
companies.improve: Post-merger, Bunge should publish a consolidated soy-origination map and a single EUDR-traceability standard across the legacy Bunge and Viterra networks; its Cerrado exposure is among the largest of any trader and warrants biome-level disclosure.

companies.name: Louis Dreyfus Company (LDC)
companies.metric: Group revenue ~US$50bn (FY2024); oilseeds (incl. soy) a core platform; major South American origination.
companies.note: The 'D' of ABCD. Large Brazil/Argentina soybean origination, crushing and export terminals; privately held with limited per-commodity disclosure.
companies.improve: LDC should disclose soy-origination volumes by Brazilian biome and the audited share of its supply under deforestation-free monitoring, plus EUDR-compliance timelines, to match the transparency demanded of listed peers.

companies.name: COFCO International
companies.metric: Handled ~108 Mt of commodities on ~US$38.5bn revenue (FY2024); the trading arm of China's state agri-giant, central to the Brazil-China soy axis.
companies.note: The key Chinese-owned trader on the Brazil-China route; reports 99% of its 2024 Brazil soy sourcing as deforestation/conversion-free, and is investing ~US$400m in a Rondonopolis crush expansion (COFCO Intl).
companies.improve: COFCO should extend its DCF-verification claim to full third-party audit and publish indirect-supplier (multi-tier) traceability, given its pivotal role moving Brazilian beans to China; concentration on a single Brazil-China corridor is also a structural risk worth quantifying.

companies.name: Amaggi
companies.metric: Brazil's largest domestically-owned soy producer-trader; significant Mato Grosso production, origination and logistics.
companies.note: A major Brazilian soy originator/exporter (and large grower in its own right), important to the Brazil-China and Brazil-EU flows alongside the ABCD (ABIOVE/company basis).
companies.improve: As a producer-trader concentrated in Mato Grosso, Amaggi should publish farm-level deforestation and Cerrado-conversion monitoring for both own-production and third-party sourcing, plus an EUDR roadmap, to retain access to the EU market.

global.note: World soybean (HS 1201) totals, kt, USDA FAS PSD Oilseeds. MY2024/25 marketing-year basis: world production ~420 Mt (record, driven by Brazil ~169 Mt + US ~119 Mt + Argentina ~49 Mt), world bean exports ~181 Mt. Years labelled by the start year of the split marketing year. Earlier years reflect the 2021/22 South American drought dip in production.

forecast.method: Projected 2030 value = 2024/25 value x (1 + CAGR)^6, per metric. Net = projected production - projected consumption. CAGR figures are reasoned assumptions inside the OECD-FAO Agricultural Outlook 2024-2033 and USDA-to-2034 envelopes (global soy demand +~1.3%/yr, South American area expansion continuing, China import growth slowing). Stated openly so they can be challenged.

scenarios.label: Brazil drought cuts the crop ~20%
scenarios.note: Brazil is ~37% of world output and ~60% of world bean exports; a La Nina / Cerrado-Matopiba drought of the 2021/22 type can cut the crop 15-25%, spiking China's import bill and global prices.

scenarios.label: US-China tariff war zeroes US beans to China
scenarios.note: China bought ~22-27 Mt of US beans in 2024 (~half of US exports); a tariff/retaliation freeze (as seen late-2025) redirects US beans to the EU/Mexico/SE Asia at a discount and hands China share to Brazil. Models a ~50% hit to US export demand.

scenarios.label: Argentina crush/export-tax disruption
scenarios.note: Argentina is the world's #1 soymeal & soyoil exporter (~40 Mt crush). A strike, drought, or export-tax/peso shock cutting crush ~30% tightens global meal supply and raises feed costs worldwide.

scenarios.label: China demand falls ~15% (herd/biofuel shift)
scenarios.note: China is ~60% of world bean imports; an African Swine Fever hog-herd contraction or a shift in crush/meal-inclusion policy cutting imports ~15% would slash Brazilian and US export demand and global prices.

scenarios.label: Parana/Mississippi low-water logistics shock
scenarios.note: Low water on the Parana-Paraguay waterway (Paraguay/Argentina beans) or the Mississippi (US Gulf exports) repeatedly raises freight and strands ~10% of exportable supply for a season (USDA AMS transport reports).

scenarios.label: EUDR tightening reshapes Brazil-EU soy
scenarios.note: The EU Deforestation Regulation requires deforestation-free traceability; partial non-compliance could cut ~10% of Brazil's ~5 Mt of beans to the EU, redirecting it to China and lifting demand for certified Canadian/Ukrainian beans.
